bug_semantics: In the function-typed asynchronous key-resolver path, a resolver result of `''` is converted to `Buffer.alloc(0)` and a zero-length Buffer is treated as a non-PEM symmetric key, so the default algorithm set becomes HS256/HS384/HS512. The verifier then calls `createSecretKey` with that empty Buffer; the resulting truthy KeyObject bypasses `verifyToken`'s Buffer-length missing-key check. Node accepts the empty HMAC secret, so an unauthenticated attacker can compute the matching HMAC over an arbitrary JWT header and payload and have the forged claims accepted. A zero-length Buffer return is equivalent; null and undefined do not reach this path.
flaw_origin: Commit e3ff09f07b55414e1fdaad2b8f225aa94832b45a changed the already-existing async resolver from `verifyToken(keyToBuffer(currentKey), ...)` to a new algorithm-detection and key-object preparation flow. It introduced `prepareKeyOrSecret`, classified non-PEM resolver bytes as HMAC, and converted those bytes with `createSecretKey` before `verifyToken` checked key presence. In direct parent a750d50bd339b0f01cd74dd8e029a51f0a5c1c16, `keyToBuffer('')` remained a zero-length Buffer and `verifyToken` rejected a signed token because `hasKey` was zero. Thus e3ff09f07b55414e1fdaad2b8f225aa94832b45a is the smallest commit that first created the bypass; 5844024ee7e2cdbbde27b4bd96dde7f3bc692713 later made key-object creation unconditional but did not originate the flaw.
ai_marker: absent — the exact BIC commit object names author `Shogun <shogun@cowtech.it>` and committer `Shogun <shogun@cowtech.it>` and contains only the message `feat: Use newer crypto features if available.`; there is no `Co-Authored-By`, `Generated-with`, or other trailer, and neither identity is a bot.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/nearform/fast-jwt/security/advisories/GHSA-gmvf-9v4p-v8jc describes the empty-string/zero-length-Buffer async-resolver attack, identifies `src/verifier.js` and `src/crypto.js`, demonstrates attacker-computable empty-key HMACs, and declares affected versions `<= 6.2.3` and patched version `6.2.4`.

History mining with `git log -L :prepareKeyOrSecret:src/verifier.js`, `git log -L 425,468:src/verifier.js`, and `git log -S` traces the causal rewrite to https://github.com/nearform/fast-jwt/commit/e3ff09f07b55414e1fdaad2b8f225aa94832b45a. Its diff adds `src/verifier.js:35-46` (`prepareKeyOrSecret`) and changes the async flow around original lines 287-313 from `verifyToken(keyToBuffer(currentKey), ...)` to string-to-Buffer conversion, `detectPublicKeyAlgorithms`, default-algorithm assignment, `prepareKeyOrSecret`, and then `verifyToken`.

At the BIC, `src/crypto.js:153-158` returns `hsAlgorithms` for a non-PEM key, while `src/crypto.js:296-310` verifies HS signatures by comparing `createHmac(alg, key).update(input).digest()` to the supplied signature. `src/crypto.js:22` sets `useNewCrypto` from availability of direct crypto signing, and `src/verifier.js:40-43` creates a secret KeyObject on that path without checking length.

Direct-parent tree verification: `git cat-file commit e3ff09f07b55414e1fdaad2b8f225aa94832b45a` gives sole parent a750d50bd339b0f01cd74dd8e029a51f0a5c1c16. In that parent, `src/utils.js:8-17` converts a string to a Buffer without creating a KeyObject; `src/verifier.js:121-135` computes `hasKey = key instanceof Buffer ? key.length : !!key` and throws missing-key for a signature with a zero-length Buffer; and `src/verifier.js:243-256` passes `keyToBuffer(currentKey)` directly to that check. The BIC diff proves the vulnerable key-object preparation and algorithm-assignment lines are absent from the direct parent. Parent URL: https://github.com/nearform/fast-jwt/commit/a750d50bd339b0f01cd74dd8e029a51f0a5c1c16.

Tag containment establishes the lower lifecycle boundary: `git tag --contains e3ff09f07b55414e1fdaad2b8f225aa94832b45a --sort=version:refname` starts at the repository's first release tag, v0.1.0 (878469bd124161f35b43b38575f9d8a237c65061), and includes every release through vulnerable v6.2.3 (ab7e46cd66b1ddff689c0b91a0392fef52a37df6). This is consistent with the advisory's unbounded-lower affected range `<= 6.2.3`.

The direct remediation commit is https://github.com/nearform/fast-jwt/commit/4e5b5708b6a9bfa5b06b5b10f888084b754c740d, whose sole parent is the v6.2.3 tag commit ab7e46cd66b1ddff689c0b91a0392fef52a37df6. Its `src/verifier.js` diff adds `if (isSecret && key.length === 0) throw FAST_JWT_INVALID_KEY` before `createSecretKey`; searching the parent for `key.length === 0` returns no match. The same commit adds the GHSA regression block at `test/verifier.spec.js:2145-2263`, covering empty strings, empty Buffers, promise/callback/JWKS resolver forms, HS256/384/512, and explicit/mixed algorithm lists.

Release ancestry is linear: v6.2.3 ab7e46cd66b1ddff689c0b91a0392fef52a37df6 -> direct fix 4e5b5708b6a9bfa5b06b5b10f888084b754c740d -> v6.2.4 release commit 044bf42c8e0a2eda8afc0819f97ae435c4214e3c. The v6.2.4 tree contains the new guard at `src/verifier.js:38-40`. First-party PR https://github.com/nearform/fast-jwt/pull/610 reports that the advisory PoC reproduced before the patch and was rejected with `FAST_JWT_INVALID_KEY` afterward; first-party release https://github.com/nearform/fast-jwt/releases/tag/v6.2.4 lists this fix as the release change.

BIC-only attribution proof: `git cat-file commit e3ff09f07b55414e1fdaad2b8f225aa94832b45a` shows tree ccd8d38597c4a580dc82d684a56285b0f3481146, one parent, human author/committer Shogun, and no trailers or bot identity. The plain one-parent commit is not a squash aggregate, so no decomposition is applicable.
reasoning: The advisory's attack path depends on an async resolver result that remains acceptable long enough to become an HMAC KeyObject. Earlier commit da11251e66e414eca89a9bee8179e86b6efff09f added the async resolver, but its direct Buffer path retained an effective zero-length check, so it is not the BIC. The `-L`, `-S`, blame, and parent-diff evidence converge on e3ff09f07b55414e1fdaad2b8f225aa94832b45a: that commit first inserted algorithm inference plus empty-secret KeyObject creation ahead of the presence check. Its direct parent demonstrably lacks that mechanism and rejects the empty Buffer, and the BIC precedes the first release tag, matching the advisory's entire `<= 6.2.3` affected range. Commit 4e5b5708b6a9bfa5b06b5b10f888084b754c740d directly closes the primitive by rejecting a zero-length symmetric key before `createSecretKey`, and it is contained in the first patched release v6.2.4. Under the required BIC-only attribution rule, the BIC's human author/committer and marker-free commit object establish NOT_AI; attribution signals on any later commit are irrelevant.
